one_month_reasoning: In the window: Q1 FY2027 results Wed 2026-11-04 after the close (guide $2.2-2.4B / $1.85-2.05; my build 2,370 / 2.07, Street 2.30B / 1.97), and the call's first read on Marvell-Lumentum (new laser LTAs) and CPO timing; NVIDIA results in late November; AAOI's Q3 print in early November. Read-across from the chain is positive: Lumentum's Sep quarter +25.5% q/q with a guide to ~$1.6B, Innolight Q3 +172% y/y, Corning optical +15% q/q, so a beat-and-raise is likely (COHR beat its revenue midpoint 4 of 4 quarters). Against it: the stock already rebounded ~5% on 11-03, optics names have sold off on beats this year, and the AI-tech tape is fragile. So a near-symmetric lognormal with a small positive drift (median ~$212.5, +1%) and a monthly sigma of ~19%, below annual vol/3.5 (25%) because the 89% realised figure includes the spring crash, but above a normal month because of the print.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued. The discount that remains is the persistent part of today's gap (k=0.8) plus 1 turn for CPO cannibalisation of pluggables after 2028 and COHR's falling share of the market (capture 21% -> 15%) against faster-growing Chinese module makers; COHR also carries net debt and a book NCI that FN, CRDO and CIEN do not.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 6 whole-company peers. LITE and MRVL are deal-priced (LITE pegged to 4.5 MRVL; LITE's 27.7x NTM is context only), ALAB (56x, fabless PCIe/CXL retimers) is not the same business, Innolight/Eoptolink are excluded as China-listed, and IPGP/MKSI/NOVT match only Industrial (~15% of FY28 revenue). No other listed optical-component makers of comparable size exist outside China/Japan conglomerates (Sumitomo, Mitsubishi Electric: optics is a small segment).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$135 (near the 52-week low of $123.75 and ~10x my FY28 EPS) the market would be pricing an AI-optics digestion or a loss of COHR's position in 1.6T/CPO lasers (e.g. NVIDIA or a top-2 hyperscaler shifting volume to Innolight/Eoptolink or a Marvell-Lumentum bundle), not ordinary volatility in an 89%-vol stock; it sits just above my P10, so trading there means the downside story is happening.

reasoning: Industry lane: I checked COHR's position against the chain. Market: LightCounting has Ethernet optics +120% in 2026 and +76% in 2027 (assuming capex +50%), slowing to ~20% by 2031, and warns of a possible 2027-30 correction; Q3 hyperscaler calls (Oct 30) keep 2027 capex rising (Alphabet 'significantly', Amazon 'meaningfully more') though Microsoft trimmed CY26 to ~$170B; the standing capex file's base (Big-4 2027 ~$1.08T) agrees. Supply: Lumentum ships >30% below demand and AAOI sees demand above capacity through mid-2027; COHR's InP output doubles by Dec-26 and again by end-2027. Share: competitors are growing much faster (Innolight Q3 +172% y/y to RMB 27.8B, Q2 +192%; LITE +136% y/y; Eoptolink Q2 +109%) than COHR D&C (+59% in Q4 FY26), so capture keeps falling; I trimmed FY28-29 capture 3% from the thread set and held FY29 D&C margin at 27.0% as shortage pricing fades. Corning (+44% optical) and Fabrinet (DC +68%) confirm broad demand. The build gives FY27 EPS 9.87 (above Zacks-basis 8.71; ~in line company basis) and FY28 12.8 (~7% below company-basis Street ~13.9-14.1 because of the capture trim). Valuation: six whole-company optical-interconnect peers, median NTM P/E 25.3x; own 19.0x; k=0.8 exit 20.1x, less 1 turn for CPO/digestion risk = 19x on horizon NTM EPS ~13.75, plus the probability-weighted Marvell-Lumentum step ($5/share); a 0.25-weight mid-cycle leg (21% margin, 20x) pulls the blend down. Scenarios move the drivers the playbook names (capture, margin, Industrial) and the multiple; the downside is deliberately fatter (P10 ~$127, near the 52-week low of $123.75) for a cyclical with 89% realised vol. Research limited to ~14 searches/fetches; X/Substack not used. The mid-cycle custom leg is not driver-linked.

model_inputs.structure_note: Starts from the thread's proposed quarterly driver set (driver_models/COHR/quarterly/set.json): D&C = LightCounting AI-cluster Ethernet optics market x dc_capture (+ lite_shift hook), Industrial = ind_rev x ind_margin, corporate constant. My changes: dc_capture -3% in every FY2028-29 quarter (FY28 15.7% vs 16.1%) and dc_margin 27.0% in FY2029 (vs 27.5%): competitor evidence shows COHR losing share faster than it can add capacity (Innolight Q3 +172% y/y, LITE +136% y/y vs COHR D&C +59% y/y in Q4 FY26) and the final year must be mid-cycle, not peak shortage pricing. dc_capture FY27 and ind_rev / ind_margin kept as the set has them. sbc_treatment set to dilution (adjusted EBIT ex SBC; shares +1%/yr) so SBC is counted once. Value carried by the NTM P/E leg (0.75) on the build's own non-GAAP EPS, plus a mid-cycle normalised-earnings custom leg (0.25, not driver-linked) and a probability-weighted Marvell-Lumentum post-NTM adjustment. No DCF (policy); no SOTP leg because forward segment multiples for Industrial peers are P/E only and Industrial is 15% of FY28 revenue (MKSI/IPGP/NOVT median 32.9x would add ~$2-3/share vs the blended P/E: noted, not booked).

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: whole-company optical-interconnect peers FN AAOI CRDO CIEN GLW MTSI: median NTM P/E 25.3x (peers.md); own 19.0x on company non-GAAP NTM; k=0.8 exit 20.1x, less 1.0 turn for post-horizon CPO and digestion risk (long_dated_risks) = 19.0x

adjustments.name: Marvell-Lumentum share shift after the horizon NTM year (if close, ramp to run-rate)
adjustments.note: Run-rate op income +136/yr if the deal closes (share_shift appraisal) x (1-0.19) = 110 after tax, less ~3 already in the horizon NTM year = 107; capitalised at 19x = 2,036; ramp FY29-FY31 and 10%/yr equity discount for ~2.5 years after the horizon (x0.79) = 1,610; industry haircut x0.87 (Counterpoint: Mitsubishi/Sumitomo are the cleaner merchant-laser winners, COHR buys LITE EMLs and Marvell DSPs) = 1,400. x p_close 0.75 = 1,050 ($5.1/share).

custom.name: Mid-cycle EPS x through-cycle P/E (playbook normalised-earnings cross-check)
custom.explanation: FY2028 model revenue 13,527 x mid-cycle non-GAAP operating margin 21.0% (FY26 actual 20.5% = 1,456.9/7,118.2; model FY28 24.5% is near a shortage-cycle peak) = 2,841; less interest 45 (5.7% on ~782 net debt at the horizon), x (1-0.19), / 204.9 horizon shares = 11.05; x 20.0x (between the 19x NTM exit and the 25.3x peer median: through-cycle EPS deserves a higher multiple than peak NTM EPS) = 221; + 5.1/share Marvell-Lumentum adjustment = 226. Not driver-linked.

model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) the -1.0 turn on the exit P/E (20.1x by the k=0.8 rule -> 19.0x) for post-horizon CPO cannibalisation and 2028 digestion risk moves the research target about -5% (~-$13/share); (2) dc_capture FY28-29 -3% vs the thread set moves it about -3%; (3) mid-cycle leg at 0.25 weight lowers the blend ~-$10. No financing event above 20%: the $2B NVIDIA placement closed (in shares and net debt); no ATM or convertible plan found (below 20%). Engine EPS omits the ~+0.01/qtr NCI add-back.
